definition: The standard classifier behind most of this archive's probes, and across 4 sources notable mainly for how often the simple baseline is competitive. Two instances. A term-frequency baseline with logistic regression reaches 0.894 AUC on one concept -- above every configuration of a kernel-based alternative -- while remaining 2.0 accuracy points behind the best internal-state probe there and 6.0 to 6.9 behind on two others, which is the right way to report a margin: against a text-only baseline that could explain it. And in trajectory-geometry work an ordinary logistic probe on the final hidden state is within a few thousandths of AUROC of a trajectory method on three of six benchmarks, so the general claim is carried by a minority. The archive's practice note is that a probe result is uninterpretable without both a surface-feature baseline and a permutation null, particularly where the feature dimension exceeds the sample count.

evidence.note: Holds one completed reasoning run fixed and varies only what a monitor is allowed to inspect — response, self-summary, full trace, internals — and finds the summary's value nearly vanishes once the monitor already has the prompt, so monitorability is a property of the display and the reader jointly rather than of the text.
evidence.title: How Much Does a Reasoning Summary Reveal? An Observability Ladder for Large Language Models

evidence.note: Trains a difference-of-means direction on short- versus long-horizon answer continuations and steers along it, shifting binary temporal choices, moving the monetary indifference threshold on an untrained task by a factor of 56 at a ten-year delay, and changing a planning benchmark — with matched-norm random controls and an unusually candid account of what the direction may actually encode.
evidence.title: Intertemporal Preference Steering in Qwen3 via Contrastive Activation Addition

evidence.note: Compares linear probes against RFM-derived concept vectors for reading how much a sentence concerns a concept out of a frozen LLM's activations, on a human-annotated ESG benchmark, and finds the simpler probe consistently stronger.
evidence.title: Measuring Concept Content in Text from LLM Activations: ESG Evidence from Concept Vectors and Linear Probes

evidence.note: Shows that which layers a steering vector should be injected at is a property of the individual input rather than of the task, that a greedy per-input rule reaches the exhaustive optimum for structural reasons, and that a label-free predictor trained to imitate that rule recovers most of the oracle at deployment.
evidence.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models

name: logistic regression
